title: Deadline-aware speculative kernel fallback and KV-lease RFC
body:
Purpose:
This RFC defines a deadline-aware speculative decoding mode that couples opportunistic kernel selection with a lightweight KV-lease mechanism. The goal is to reduce tail latency while bounding risk to model output correctness and KV cache consistency during kernel switchover and aggressive prefetching. This document contains design details, acceptance criteria for model onboarding, a rollback checklist, and the core metrics to gate rollout.

Context / motivation:
- We observed spiky P99s for interactive chat workloads when our preferred low-latency kernels occasionally underperform on certain prompt shapes (long context, unusual tokenization).
- Full kernel fallback is expensive (warmup cost and token re-emit complexity) and KV cache inconsistency during mid-request switching can cause corrupted continuations or repeats.
- Prior work in the team focused on proactive prefetch and conservative fallback; this RFC explores a middle ground: try a speculative fast-path kernel under a soft deadline and, if it misses latency expectations or produces divergence risk signals, fallback deterministically with minimal client-visible effect.

Key ideas (high level):
1) Deadline window: every decode invocation attaches a soft deadline derived from routing SLO (e.g., 120ms remaining for next token). We track remaining allowed time at each token emission.
2) Speculative kernel candidate set: for each model variant the controller maintains an ordered list of kernels with metadata (expected per-token latency distribution, warmup overhead, correctness-safety-tag). Candidates labeled "speculative" are fast but slightly riskier on some inputs (e.g., quantized int4 kernels for long prefix patterns).
3) Two-phase emission with no client replay: We emit tokens from the speculative kernel immediately but keep the authoritative token stream in a guarded buffer. If we later decide a rollback is required we append compensating actions (recompute on fallback kernel and emit correction tokens) in a way that preserves continuity for streaming clients (see runbook).
4) KV-lease semantics: to avoid stale KV reads/writes during speculative kernel use, we introduce a short-lived per-request KV-lease token. Kernels operating under a lease may provisionally update KV. If the request falls back, the provisional mutations are revoked and the fallback kernel applies canonical updates. Leases expire automatically if fallback occurs or on completion.

Detailed design:
- Controller flow:
  * Request arrives with model_id, pinned_version, routing_slo_ms. Controller computes token_deadline_ms = now + routing_slo_ms - reserved_margin_ms.
  * Look up candidate kernels and select first speculative candidate whose warmup+mean_latency <= token_deadline_ms. If none, select conservative kernel.
  * Allocate KV-lease id (uuid) and write lease header into request metadata; attach expected lease ttl (default 300ms).
  * Start speculative kernel task, stream speculative tokens to client via streaming buffer that marks tokens as provisional.
  * In parallel, run a lightweight verifier that checks risk signals (per-token logprob delta vs baseline model, divergence heuristics, kernel internal divergence flags). If verifier trips before token_deadline_ms, abort speculative kernel, start fallback kernel and re-emit corrected tokens.

- Token emission semantics and no-replay guarantee:
  * We must avoid literal client-level replays that break streaming clients. The streaming buffer encodes provisional tokens along with sequence ids and an instruction tag (provisional / confirmed / correction).
  * If fallback occurs, the controller emits a small correction span: a rewind marker + canonical tokens computed by the fallback kernel. Streaming clients are expected to treat the rewind marker as a small splice; SDKs will translate it into a minimal client-side delta event.

- KV-lease lifecycle and constraints:
  * A KV-lease id is issued per request. Provisional writes include lease id and are marked as provisional in the KV store. Reads check both canonical and provisional layers and merge deterministically (provisional wins for same request id).
  * If fallback occurs, provisional layer is discarded. If speculative path completes and tokens are confirmed, provisional mutations are committed atomically (lease -> commit).
  * Leases enforce a max mutation size and scope: no cross-session global changes to avoid wide blast radius. Leases are intended for per-request short-lived KV (prefix caches, ephemeral reranking contexts), not persistent customer state.

Acceptance criteria for model onboarding (draft):
- Functional correctness: no silent corruption or repeated tokens in > 1e-4 of requests in synthetic fuzz tests covering 100k randomized prompt shapes.
- Latency improvement: P95 per-token improved by at least 10% for the targeted workload cohort vs baseline conservative kernel.
- Cost regression: median GPU token cost must not increase > 5% for the same traffic split.
- KV safety: rollback rate (requests which had provisional writes discarded) < 0.3% in steady state for accepted models.
- Regression testing: run the model against the canonical eval set used by model acceptance and ensure output-level BLEU/ROUGE/behavioral regressions are within preestablished tolerances.

Metrics (instrumentation and definitions):
- speculative_selection_rate: ratio of requests that were assigned a speculative kernel candidate (per model_id).
- speculative_confirm_rate: fraction of speculative runs that completed without fallback (per model_id, per kernel).
- fallback_rate: fraction of requests that triggered fallback within the request lifespan.
- correction_span_tokens: number of correction tokens emitted per fallback (mean, p95).
- kv_lease_issued: count of leases created.
- kv_lease_discard_rate: fraction of leases whose provisional mutations were discarded due to fallback.
- per_token_latency_p50_p95_p99: separate series for speculative and conservative kernels.
- model_divergence_alarm: rate of verifier-triggered divergence signals per 10k tokens.
- user-visible-error_rate: client errors or malformed output incidents post-speculation.

Testing plan (staged):
1) Unit tests: kernel adapter mocks, lease lifecycle, streaming buffer behavior with scripted rewrite scenarios.
2) Local integration: run a two-kernel simulated runtime where kernel A is fast but nondeterministic (inject failures/delays) and kernel B is canonical. Validate splice markers and lease commit/discard paths.
3) Load test: synthetic traffic reproducing target prompt distributions; measure speculative_confirm_rate and fallback_rate under load and with rolling kernel perturbations.
4) Canary: 1% traffic onhost, with tracing and automatic rollback if any of the hard gates trip (fallback_rate > 3% sustained for 5m, user-visible-error_rate > baseline+0.05%).
5) Regional ramp: expand to 10% -> 30% -> 100% with post-mortem after each ramp and extended monitoring window.

Rollback and emergency procedures:
- Automated rollback gate: if fallback_rate or kv_lease_discard_rate crosses configured thresholds, autoscaler triggers immediate kernel selection policy rollback to conservative kernel and sets speculation disabled flag for affected model_ids.
- Manual rollback steps for SRE/owners:
  1) Flip feature flag: disable deadline-aware speculative selection for model/version in the controller.
  2) Invalidate all outstanding KV-leases (mark them revoked) and force commit/abort per policy (by default abort).
  3) Recompute any in-flight requests that had provisional tokens retained longer than safe window (run repair job to detect and annotate affected sessions).
  4) Post-incident: collect full traces for a sample of failed sessions, and add failing prompt shapes to the model onboarding negative test suite.

Observability and logging changes needed:
- New trace spans: speculative_select, lease_grant, verify_run, fallback_initiate, correction_emit, lease_commit, lease_abort.
- Event dimensions: model_id, kernel_id, lease_id, request_id, shard_id, region.
- SLO dashboards: per-model speculative_confirm_rate, fallback_rate, and kv_lease_discard_rate. Export alarms to PagerDuty when p99 per-token latency regresses > 40ms vs baseline or when user-visible-error_rate spikes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: client SDKs not handling rewind/correction markers correctly -> mitigation: ship SDK patch before wide rollout; default to disable streaming splice for older SDKs by user-agent gating.
- Risk: provisional KV writes used by downstream systems inappropriately -> mitigation: write-scope enforcement on lease manager and telemetry to detect cross-lease ownership.
- Risk: verifier false-positives causing unnecessary fallback -> mitigation: conservative verifier thresholds in canary; build quick retraining loop for verifier thresholds per-model.

Open questions / next steps:
- Should the verifier run on a sampled subset of tokens (every Nth token) for very long generations to reduce compute overhead?
- Lease TTL tuning: default 300ms was chosen conservatively — recommend experiments at 100ms / 500ms for different workload classes.
- SDK behavior: define a minimal codec for splice markers and roll out versioned event contracts.

Appendix: operator checklist for canary -> prod
- Pre-roll: ensure model has signed-off acceptance test bundle and negative example list.
- Start canary at 1% traffic with verbose tracing.
- After 30 minutes stable, check:
  * fallback_rate < 1%
  * speculative_confirm_rate > 80%
  * kv_lease_discard_rate < 0.2%
  * no user-visible-error_rate regressions
- If a gate fails during ramp, run immediate rollback steps and open incident.

Notes from preliminary experiments:
- In our small internal experiment with a T5-style quantized kernel, speculative_confirm_rate was 86% and P95 improved by ~15ms for short-chat workloads, but correction_span_tokens averaged 3 tokens on fallbacks. That was considered acceptable but needs more cross-model validation.

Contact and ownership:
- Primary owner: Daniela Ruiz (eng-serving-runtime)
- Reviewer leads: Marcus Lee (serving-runtime), Priya Nair (kernel team), Omar Singh (SRE)

End of RFC.
